findings.title: Narrow the queued-work acceptance check to false queued-work claims
findings.trigger: An executor runs the prescribed Phase 90-07 acceptance command.
findings.execution_path: The recursive grep scans all triggarr source and matches db.py:1621: 'Rows with no stable ID are never selected by any'.
findings.consequence: The required 'prints nothing' criterion fails on correct implementation documentation, causing a false acceptance failure or prompting removal of an accurate safety explanation.
findings.evidence: The exact command returned the db.py:1621 match. That statement concerns unidentified rows, not stale queued work, and agrees with the stable-ID-only tracking guards.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the check to the scheduled/manual search and removal comment blocks, or replace the broad phrase ban with a check specifically targeting the incorrect queued-work claim. Exclude generated bytecode from source checks.
findings.reproduction_command: grep -rniE "never selected|nobody selects|selected by nobody" triggarr/

limitations: Pytest was not independently rerun: the read-only sandbox prevents the suite's temporary database/configuration writes. The harness evidence identifies the exact inspected head and reports exit 0, 3520 passed, 1 skipped.
No live UI, external Arr server or real disk-failure testing was performed; these paths were assessed through source and regression-test inspection.
